newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close firmer, boosted by dollar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close firmer, boosted by dollar.

text.p: French shares ended higher on Wednesday, but just below the key 2,600 level, as continued dollar strength supported the market, traders said.
Banking and financial stocks led the risers, with the market continuing to see robust volumes.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.24 points or 0.67 percent at 2,599.33. The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,605 from 2,591 on Tuesday's close.

The market came off its highs following Bundesbank comments that the dollar correction was over, but despite that verbal intervention, sentiment on the U.S. currency remained buoyant and French stocks stayed bullish.

Cie Bancaire and Cetelem were among strong risers, up respectively 2.86 percent at 720 francs and 1.3 percent at 700, helped by rumours Bancaire could make a buy out offer for Cetelem on a one-for-one share offer.
BNP gains 3.49 percent to 237.5, after triggering strong buying orders at 231 francs, as well on hopes of strong 1996 profits.
Axa fell 1.82 percent to 372.9 francs, hit by disappointment over a surprise drop in fourth quarter net profit at its U.S. Equitable unit.
L'Oreal rises 3.01 percent at 2,018 francs and Synthelabo advances 3.77 percent amid familiar rumours of a sale of Synthelabo by its parent.

Pechiney rises 5.97 percent at 257.3, and Usinor-Sacilor, up 0.31 percent 79.7 but off highs. Both saw big rises after attracting buying interest for cyclical stocks and after having underperformed the market.
